How a session runs

Assess. Drill. Play.

Every 60-minute session follows the same three parts, so you always know what is coming and what you are working on.

  1. 1

    Assess

    We rally a few balls so I can see your grip, footwork and where the ball goes. You tell me what you want to fix.

    10 minutes
  2. 2

    Drill

    One skill at a time, with short repeated drills. I correct one thing per round so it sticks.

    30 minutes
  3. 3

    Play

    We finish with a short game, so you use the new skill under real scoring.

    20 minutes

Before your first game

Four rules to learn first

Know these and you can join any open play session without slowing the game down. Hover or tap a rule to see it on the court.

Two-bounce rule

The serve must bounce, then the return must bounce. After that, volleys are allowed.

The kitchen

No volleying while standing in the 7 foot zone by the net. You can step in to hit a ball that has bounced.

Underhand serve

Contact the ball below the waist. Serve diagonally into the opposite service box.

Score to 11

Only the serving side scores. Win by 2. Call the score as three numbers: yours, theirs, server.

Good to know

Questions before you book

I have never played. Is that okay?

Yes. First Rally assumes no experience. We start with grip and footwork, and you will be rallying by the end of the first session.

What should I bring?

Court shoes and water. Bring a paddle if you have one, and say in your request if you need one so Mark can confirm what is available.

Can I bring friends?

Yes. Sessions work for 1 to 4 players. Mention the group size when you book.
